notes: Brief built (135 rules: writing 28, student_facing 37, prompts 49, sales_copy 13, strategy_tie_in 8). Prompt-class rows judged on the one registry prompt via expanded view. Maintainer accept-notes (L57,59,61,65) found; none authorises author-we on L49, so the finding stands for the maintainer to accept-note or recast. Cross-class: L49 paragraph is verbatim team M8 with today/room edits.

resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. writing §6 (author-we ban) line 49: scope: Verified: the rule is the author-"we" ban under check_writing.md section 6 (line 73), and the line is body prose at solo.md:49. The judge reads the rule correctly, and none of its KEEP carve-outs applies. The diagnostic also fires, since "the training authors could have spent this course" reads as author-we. So the rule does fire literally. I still refute it, for three reasons.

1. The maintainer deliberately carried this paragraph. Solo L65 says "The against-interest paragraph is team M8's, with 'today' made 'this course' and 'in this room' cut." Those two edits are the only changes the maintainer authorised. The "We" was kept on purpose. Team M8 L71 records the same sentence as a dated stance beat (Antti 2026-11-13, against-interest line). The "we" is the stance: an interested speaker saying it gave up something. The judge's recast ("This course could have been one impressive agent built for you") deletes that speaker, so it is a content change to maintainer-supplied wording, not a mechanical fix.

2. The paragraph was measured. Solo L61 records a simulation in which this stance paragraph plus the M8 section took the score from 17 to 27, inside the 20-point floor. Rewording it voids that measurement. Rewording a maintainer-directed, sim-tested sentence to satisfy a lead-rule is the over-firing case in compounded/2026-08-02-content_creation-a-rule-firing-is-not-the-harm-arriving.md, where the fix degrades the artefact.

3. The harm the rule targets is "personal to someone the student does not know". That harm is thin here. The speaker is the course itself, in a single anonymous stance line. No creator name appears, and no "we built / we curate" apparatus is narrating the training. Story judges (story-depth evals) read this unnamed "we" as the intended against-interest stance beat.

Caveat: no accept-note names author-we explicitly. Solo L65 and team L71 direct the paragraph and its wording, but they do not mention the rule. If the maintainer wants it clean, the right route is an explicit accept-note in the maintainer block or a rule carve-out for the stance beat. It is not a blocking REVISE on a body that matches maintainer direction. / harm: I read the solo file, the §6 rule (check_writing.md L73), and the team M8 file. The factual claims check out: L49 quotes accurately, the rule bans author-we, none of the five KEEP carve-outs applies, and the L65 maintainer note names no author-we accept. So the rule applies. The finding fails on the harm lens.

(a) Harm: nobody in the room is worse off. The student does not read "we" as a personal claim about someone they do not know. They read the line as the course speaking. The rule's diagnostic ("sentence weird with 'the training authors'?") does fire, but the harm is tidiness, not confusion or a broken claim.

(b) The harm is a restatement of the rule. The finding says "first-person plural for the training authors, which is personal to someone the student does not know". That is §6's own wording, with no consequence beyond it.

(c) The fix has a cost. This sentence is the maintainer-named stance beat, the against-interest line. Antti set it on 2026-11-13 in the team M8 maintainer block: "'We could have spent today building you one impressive agent… the wrong thing to sell you' is the stance beat". The solo L65 note says the paragraph was carried over from team M8 on purpose, and L61 shows the sim measured it (17 without the paragraph, 27 with it, against a 20-point floor). The beat works because the authors chose against their own interest. "This course could have been one impressive agent" turns that choice into a passive hypothetical, so the stance is weaker. It also edits text that sim-tested, so a re-sim would be owed. The solo edition has no sponsor, which is why the page carries this beat.

(d) Not a no-op, but the meaning is carried only partly elsewhere. L47 and L53 do not carry the against-interest stance.

(e) Minor factual slip in the finding: L65 lists two wording edits, but the solo line differs from team M8 in three places ("today" to "this course", "sell" to "give", and "in this room" cut). This does not rescue the finding.

The team M8 file carries the same "we" with the same maintainer endorsement. The writing PASS on it dates from 2026-08-25, before the 2026-11-13 line was added, so the audit does not cover the line. Even so, maintainer-endorsed deliberate wording plus a measured beat, set against a cosmetic recast, means I cannot sustain a BLOCKING finding. If anything, this is a maintainer-block note ("author-we accepted here, stance beat") rather than a body edit.
